failure_case.cause: With category-only features, every candidate in a category has an identical score after IDF weighting. All 1,260 users have at least 19 candidates tied at their maximum score (median 3,211), so the Top-5 is determined entirely by the tie-break. This user's maximum category is Фильмы, and popularity-then-ID returns five films, none of which is a validation hit.
failure_case.training_history_flag_definition: in_training_history and personal_seen_* flags are keyed by the selected user's train_idx and describe that user's personal training history. in_training_history means that user's positive_airings > 0 for the item. global_item_coverage is separately aggregated across all training users.

global_item_coverage_definition: global_item_coverage counts distinct training users and their airings for the item across all training users, split by any-positive, >=50%, and >=80% coverage. It does not describe the selected user's history.
limitations: The light user has no primary validation positives, so AP@5 is 0 by definition for every method; this is not evidence of which method is better for light users.
Titles/categories shown are from training-period metadata only.
in_training_history is personal to the selected user; global_item_coverage is reported separately.

selection_rule.heavy: maximum distinct training programs with >=80% qualifying airings; ties by total >=80% qualifying airings then ascending user_id
selection_rule.light: minimum distinct training programs with >=80% qualifying airings among users with at least one such program; ties by total >=80% qualifying airings then ascending user_id

training_history_flag_definition: in_training_history and personal_seen_* fields use counts keyed by the selected user's train_idx; they describe that user's personal training history. in_training_history means the user has positive_airings > 0 for the item. global_item_coverage is a separate item-level calculation across all training users.

worked_ap_at_5.note: Arithmetic shown for independent checking; not claimed to be user-verified.
